requirements.evidence: .env.example:1,7-8 sets APP_NAME=PegaFila and APP_LOCALE=pt_BR; phpunit.xml:22-24 pins APP_NAME/APP_LOCALE/APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE; config/mail.php:128 selects the pegafila theme and resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/pegafila.css:240-242 applies #0f7490 to the action button; routes/web.php:13-30 defines all five named routes with guest/throttle:6,1/auth/signed; PasswordResetLinkController.php:25-31 validates the e-mail and always flashes passwords.sent; NewPasswordController.php:32-57 validates token/email/password, saves the password, rotates remember_token and fires PasswordReset; VerifyEmailController.php:19-33 checks id and hash (403 otherwise) and redirects to '/'; lang/pt_BR.json:559,804 adds both subject strings.

conventions.evidence: Pest tests, the three forced phpunit pins and the CHANGELOG entry (CHANGELOG.md:12) follow the conventions; deviations: the two auth pages duplicate the whole page shell/status/error/form markup instead of using Blade components (forgot-password.blade.php:1-66, reset-password.blade.php:1-97), and a three-field reset validation stays inline (NewPasswordController.php:32-40) where the conventions suggest a Form Request once rules grow.

security.evidence: All user output is escaped with {{ }} (reset-password.blade.php:36,46; forgot-password.blade.php:19,43), both forms have @csrf (forgot-password.blade.php:33, reset-password.blade.php:34), the verify route runs auth+signed+throttle (routes/web.php:28-30), id/hash are compared with hash_equals (VerifyEmailController.php:19-27), the broker validates the token and the Password rule enforces min 8/letters/mixedCase/numbers (NewPasswordController.php:32-40), and the reset request never reveals account existence (PasswordResetLinkController.php:31).

tests.evidence: MailThemeTest.php:7-36 covers locale/theme/brand color, PasswordResetTest.php:15-135 covers the request/response/update paths including failure cases, and EmailVerificationTest.php:28-75 covers verification and forbidden cases; however no test exercises throttle:6,1 or the guest guard (routes/web.php:13-19), and the notification test checks only the URL path, not its signature (EmailVerificationTest.php:12-26).

simplicity.evidence: Controllers are small and reuse Laravel's Password broker (PasswordResetLinkController.php:25-31, NewPasswordController.php:42-57), but the two auth views repeat the same shell/status/error/form markup (forgot-password.blade.php:1-66 vs reset-password.blade.php:1-97) and config/mail.php:134-137 adds an unused empty extensions array.

readability.evidence: Focused methods with clear names (VerifyEmailController.php:15-34, NewPasswordController.php:19-58), semantic accessible form markup with labels and Bulma classes (forgot-password.blade.php:36-62, reset-password.blade.php:55-79), and no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: env/phpunit locale pins, mail config and theme, the two password controllers, the verification controller, routes, two views, two lang entries, MustVerifyEmail on User.php:6,15, and the CHANGELOG.md:12 entry; no login/registration/Livewire/nginx/SCSS changes.

issues.explanation: The task names throttle:6,1 on password.email and guests-only reset routes, but no test exercises either middleware, so a regression in rate limiting or access control would not be caught.

The notification test checks only that the action URL contains /email/verify/{id}/, and the signed-link tests build their own URL, so nothing proves the URL produced by the notification actually satisfies the signed middleware.

The two auth pages duplicate the full HTML shell and the status/error/form-field markup instead of extracting reusable anonymous Blade components, which the conventions ask for (only layouts and UI lang files are out of scope).
A three-field validation with a complex password rule is kept inline; the conventions reserve inline validation for one or two fields and suggest a Form Request once the rules grow.
The UI feature tests assert status and key markup but not the accessible labels, although the Bulma conventions ask tests to assert accessible labels.
The new markdown config includes an empty extensions array that nothing uses, so it is speculative configuration.

review.summary: The change implements the complete pt-BR password-reset and e-mail-verification flow with the PegaFila mail theme, branded #0f7490 action buttons, all required named routes, and a broad Pest suite. It is functionally complete and secure; the remaining gaps are minor test coverage for route middleware and the signed notification URL plus duplicated auth-page markup that could use Blade components, so I would approve with nits.
